notes: Ready-to-use replacement for helped-media-transcription.blueprint.json, which ships an intentional provider placeholder.

Deepgram is used because its listen endpoint is synchronous and accepts an HTTPS audio URL directly, so no file upload is needed: POST https://api.deepgram.com/v1/listen with body {"url": "<mediaUrl>"}.

Setup: (1) open the webhook module and SELECT YOUR EXISTING 'Helped Media Transcription' webhook so MAKE_WEBHOOK_URL_MEDIA_TRANSCRIBE keeps working unchanged, (2) replace YOUR_DEEPGRAM_API_KEY with a real key, (3) click Run once, (4) verify with: npm run test:media-transcribe
This blueprint sets dlq:true so failed runs are stored under Incomplete executions — that is what makes 'Scenario failed to complete.' debuggable afterwards.
If the transcript comes back empty, open module 3 and click the transcript field in the mapping panel; Make writes the exact path for you (Make array indices are 1-based).

metadata.notes: Create or select the webhook: Helped Media Transcription.
Deepgram transcribes the short-lived signed URL. Response: results.channels.1.alternatives.1.transcript. Move the key into a Make connection/keychain instead of the header if you prefer.
Exactly the shape transcribePrivateMedia() parses: it reads result.transcript ?? result.text.
